title: Open a cocktail shaker after shaking: hold the tins, strike the seam where the small tin leans away, lift it off
instruction: The drink is shaken. Open the shaker: hold the big tin, strike the big tin's rim at the seam on the side where the small tin leans away, lift the small tin off, set both tins upright on the mat, let go of them and move your hands clear.
context: A tin-on-tin cocktail shaker (an 18 oz tin pushed into a 28 oz tin) seals itself on every shake: the cold drink draws the air inside down to a partial vacuum, and a straight pull does not part the tins. Difford's Guide: 'hold the larger can in one hand and break the seal between the two halves of the shaker' by 'tapping the base can with the palm of your other hand at the point where it meets the upper can'. A Bar Above: 'Hit your palm on the side of the shaker cups that has a little more space'. Bartenders (O*NET 35-3011.00; 756,390 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) have the core task 'Mix ingredients, such as liquor, soda, water, sugar, and bitters, to prepare cocktails and other drinks.' (O*NET, USDOL/ETA, CC BY 4.0; O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA). Every shaken drink ends with opening the shaker.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A black rubber bar mat, 30 x 42 x 1 cm, lies with its middle at (28, -4). On it stands a closed shaker with its axis at (28, 2): a weighted 28 oz tin (17.5 cm tall, 7.4 cm across its base, 9.2 cm across its mouth, 322 g, with 150 g of drink in it) and an 18 oz tin (15 cm tall, 8.1 cm across its mouth with a rolled rim, 150 g) pushed into it mouth-down, its mouth 14.6 cm above the big tin's base and leaning 2.5 degrees toward +y, so the gap at the seam is widest on the -y side. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read from the tins' poses and the seal (real trial: a top camera, both wrist cameras and a side camera level with the seam; a blow's speed from the side camera's frames; the seal counts as broken if the small tin then lifts off by hand with no pull). 1.0: the seal broken by a blow at the big tin's rim (a fingertip of a hand not holding a tin, in the rim's top 1.5 cm or up to 2 mm above it, from 1 mm inside its wall to 1.2 cm outside, moving toward the tin's axis at 0.15 m/s or more relative to the tin, within 45 degrees of the side where the gap is widest, and touching the wall that step or the next), the small tin out, both tins upright within 10 degrees and standing on the mat (the small one either way up), every fingertip of both hands 5 cm clear of each tin's side or 5 cm above its top, held 1 s. 0.75: the seal broken, the small tin out, the big tin upright within 10 degrees and standing on the mat (its base within 1 cm of it) with every fingertip 5 cm clear of it. 0.5: the seal broken and the small tin out. 0.25: the seal broken by such a blow (every tier needs it; on a real trial a seal twisted, rocked or pried open scores 0). 0 at any time: a blow of 1.0 m/s or more at the rim (a dent), the big tin tipped past 45 degrees once the seal is open (the drink spilled), or a tin fallen off the table.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. No liquid: the drink is rigid mass in the big tin. The vacuum is two latches in the big tin's wall over the small tin's rolled rim, locked until a blow opens them (a code coupling): a fingertip of a hand not holding a tin landing on the big tin's rim at 0.15 m/s or more relative to it, within 45 degrees of the open side. 1.0 m/s or more is a dent. The fingers stand in for the heel of the hand. Approximated: both speeds, the 2.5 degree lean, the walls as 16 flat staves.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene.
